steps.name: Campbell
steps.text: Really? Oripathy doesn't pass from the Infected to healthy people?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Regular contact with Oripathy patients in stable conditions does not transmit Oripathy.

steps.name: Campbell
steps.text: But how do I know if someone is infected or not?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: I've contacted the nearest Rhodes Island office. They'll be sending test kits soon—

steps.name: Campbell
steps.text: Just go home, kid, and tell your family to move as soon as you can.

steps.name: Campbell
steps.text: People are afraid that your dad will pass Oripathy onto other people. We can't afford that.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Please, Mrs. Samantha, patients who are in stable conditions are not infectious.

steps.name: Samantha
steps.text: How can you prove that?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: I come from Rhodes Island, where the Infected and non-Infected live together. Infection is not a problem, as long as the progress of Oripathy is monitored regularly.

steps.name: Samantha
steps.text: Don't play with that girl, Molly! They've got an Infected at home! You'll get the stone disease!

steps.name: Samantha's Daughter
steps.text: Stone disease?

steps.name: Samantha
steps.text: A disease where you grow rocks from your body! It hurts so much you die from the pain alone!

steps.name: Sandwheel
steps.text: Water, Honeyberry?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Thanks.

steps.name: Sandwheel
steps.text: You spent all morning talking. Did they listen?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: They will. As long as they can let go of their prejudice, there won't be any issues with the Infected here. And I won't need to be here.

steps.name: Sandwheel
steps.text: You're so patient with them.

steps.name: Sandwheel
steps.text: If my own family was chased out, there's no way I'd set aside the grudge and come back to help them with their Infected problem, no matter how many years had passed.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: It's... not that I've set it aside.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: The issue with Dad, I can understand. Hard not to panic when there's an Infected so close to you.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: But the thing with Mum, I could never...

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: I came because I want them to set their prejudices aside. I don't want another tragedy like mine to happen.

steps.name: Martenson
steps.text: No!

steps.name: Martenson
steps.text: My son's going to be a mining company manager! I can't have him living with the Infected!

steps.name: Martenson's Mother
steps.text: My son's joining the mining company! I can't have him live and eat with you people!

steps.name: Martenson's Mother
steps.text: Scram! Get out, while we're still asking nicely!

steps.name: Martenson
steps.text: We asked you to solve our Infected problem, not to preach at us!

steps.name: Martenson
steps.text: We're an important supply point for the mining company! How are we supposed to do business with those Infected making a mess every few days?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: I understand, I do.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: But think of it this way: the Infected won't do that if everyone's getting along, right?

steps.name: Martenson
steps.text: Says you! Their ringleader only came back to cause trouble because he realized he could use Originium Arts. He's a lunatic with rocks growing out of his brain!

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Why you—

steps.name: Sandwheel
steps.text: We should go, Honeyberry.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Right... okay.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Looks like two-fifths are willing to listen, two-fifths are undecided, and the last fifth is strongly opposed.

steps.name: Sandwheel
steps.text: So what's our next move?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: I think it's worth getting everyone together to talk this out.

steps.name: Sandwheel
steps.text: To be honest, the people you've categorized as 'willing to listen' seem pretty undecided to me.

steps.name: Sandwheel
steps.text: Maybe you could reveal your identity? None of them recognized you. Maybe they'll be willing to side with you for old times' sake? Or even out of guilt.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: I... don't want to do that.

steps.name: Sandwheel
steps.text: Sorry.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: But if the villagers really are as stubborn as you say...

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Anyway, let's get them together.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: ...The Infected and non-Infected can live together as long as there are proper identification, testing, and protection procedures in place.

steps.name: Martenson
steps.text: Wait, it's you!

steps.name: Martenson
steps.text: What are you doing here? Get out! You're not welcome here!

spans.text: doing here? Get out! You're not welcome here!

steps.name: Fierce Infected
steps.text: This is my home too. Who do you think you are?

steps.name: Fierce Infected
steps.text: So what's this all about? Some kinda meeting? Trying to run more Infected out of town? Hey, who the heck are you?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: I'm Operator Honeyberry, from Rhodes Island—

steps.name: Fierce Infected
steps.text: Rhodes Island? What's that? Did the mining company send you?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: We did come at the mining company's request, but we're not taking a side here. We just want to get the problem resolved.

steps.name: Fierce Infected
steps.text: Yeah right! You're just the company's hounds!

steps.name: Fierce Infected
steps.text: You're coming with me! Let's see what you're plotting!
Sandwheel tries to get to Honeyberry, but she waves him off.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Suits me just fine. I was going to visit you anyway.

steps.name: Fierce Infected
steps.text: Ha, got a big mouth on you.

steps.name: Samantha
steps.text: Gus, she's a guest. Show some respect—

steps.name: Samantha
steps.text: Eek!

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: Who's the one who needs to show respect here, huh?

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: Anyone who dares stand in my way gets it to the head!

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: We're here.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: (This is...)

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: Now spill it! Why'd they send you?!

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: What's the matter? You seemed pretty chatty back in the village.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: How did you find this place?

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: We had nowhere to go, and no one was living here. Why wouldn't we?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: The first Infected from the village used to live here with his wife and kid.

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: Don't you try to change the subject with old stories or whatever.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: I was telling the truth back there. I came to help solve your problems, Gus.

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: Solve my problems? How? I told them the rocks appeared on their own without catching it from anyone, but did they believe me?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: That's why I'm promoting knowledge about proper Oripathy prevention and treatment, so that you can go back to the village.
Two figures emerge from the shadows.

steps.name: Infected A
steps.text: Is that for real?

steps.name: Infected B
steps.text: We can go back to the village?

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: Quiet! Stay outta this!

steps.name: Infected A
steps.text: But she said—

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: How do you know she's not lying?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: I was telling the truth.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: And where's your sister, Gus?

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: H-How did you know I had a sister?

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: Argh, whatever.

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: Lydia's in her room.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Hello, Lydia. Are you there?

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Who's that? Another exile from the village? How is Carl?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: I'm Operator Honeyberry, from Rhodes Island. I'm here to help.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Hello, Honeyberry—

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Wait, no— *cough* You're—

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Is it really you?! Zoey Perris?!

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Lydia... you...

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Yes, we used to play together all the time. Even if the rest of the village forgot about me, you never...

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Of course I'd never forget my best mate... *cough*, *cough*

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: What about Mr. and Mrs. Perris? Did they go to Rhodes Island with you?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Mum's living with me on Rhodes Island. Dad passed away soon after he was chased out.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: ...I'm sorry.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: It's okay. I still remember how you used to bring us stuff after we were exiled.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: But after Grandpa found out...

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Let's talk about you first. You don't look too good...

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: I've been feeling ill ever since I was exiled. Colds, headaches, occasional vomiting...

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: (Could Lydia be like Mum...?)

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Let me do a quick checkup.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: The quick test strips show an extremely low chance that you have Oripathy. I didn't see signs of any organic diseases either.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: No Originium crystals on the body surface... I'll check with more precise equipment.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: The results show you don't have Oripathy.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: I see...

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: (She doesn't seem happy about it...)

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Can I ask you something? Have you felt stressed lately?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Are you sure?

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: There's just someone in the village I'm concerned about...

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: (Someone in the village? Is it the name she said before she recognized me?)

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Carl? Mr. Martenson's son?
Her childhood friend looks at her with a shocked expression, then tears begin flowing from her eyes.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Carl and I were going to tell Mr. Martenson about our relationship and get engaged. And then Gus got sick.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Carl and I had been looking forward to it and preparing for so long... and then...

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Lydia...

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: I might never see him again. When I think about that, I...

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Ugh—

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Zoey, I'm feeling sick... I think I might throw up. Stay away...

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Why would you say that?!

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Gus, Gus! Are you there?

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: What's going on?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: See if there's a kind of grass in the garden that's about the height of a human palm, with slightly red-tipped leaves growing in opposing pairs!

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: Let me see... yeah. What about it?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Grab a few of them! Lydia's about to throw up, and that's a herb that can help.

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: What? I'll get right on it!

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: How do you feel?

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Zoey... much better. Thank you.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: This is just for emergencies, though.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Whether it's some kind of organic disease I've never heard of, or the result of psychological factors, the herb will only alleviate the symptoms, not the cause.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: My mum was in a situation just like yours. She got much better after the psychological problems went away.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: And how'd she do that?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: I grew up and reduced the burden on her. She didn't have to worry about tomorrow's bread, and our situation got better as well, so she got better on her own.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: But how can I not worry?

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: *cough,* *cough!*

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: The villagers see me as the family of an Infected. Gus is afraid they'll hurt me, and I... I'm like this.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: I don't care if I'm infected, and I don't care what they think. All I want is to see Carl again... one more time...

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: I have an idea.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: I know of a herb that grows around here that can give you a fever, without seriously threatening your health.

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: What's going on? Why does Lydia have a fever?!

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: The reason isn't important right now. What's important is that Lydia wants to go back to the village.

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: I know that! How many times do you think she's told me?! It's always Carl this, Carl that! He's such a fraud!

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: He's not even showing his face at a time like this! That tells me all I need to know.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Lydia's feelings are real, though. Otherwise she wouldn't be so ill.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: No matter how much you hate Carl and the villagers, think of your sister. It's not Oripathy she has, it's an illness of the mind!

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: The mind...

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: If you're really worried about her, let her go back. I can guarantee that the villagers won't harm her.

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: So... what? She sees that fraud and gets better. What then?

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: The village will never accept her, and it's not like Carl would ever come live with us. She'll still suffer in the end!

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: So you're just going to watch her suffer from the fever she's got right now?

steps.name: Lydia's Grandfather
steps.text: Perris, the whole village will be destroyed if your Oripathy spreads.

steps.name: Honeyberry's Father
steps.text: But my wife and daughter are healthy! They don't have any stones on them!

steps.name: Lydia's Grandfather
steps.text: Better safe than sorry. It's all for the village, you know.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Gus, I came here to dispel the village's fear, and the prejudices you have of each other.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Sure, some rejected me, but others were willing to listen.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Just try it. For yourself, for Lydia, and for them.

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: I can see you mean what you're saying, but I still don't believe those bastards can actually let go of their prejudices.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: You mean...

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: You can try, but on one condition.

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: Most of the villagers don't know about Lydia and Carl. Martenson is only thinking about his son's career, and he sure as hell wasn't gonna go around and tell people about it.

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: You're not allowed to bring up Carl's name in the village. I want to see him step up on his own.

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: Otherwise, he'd only do it because he didn't have a choice.

steps.name: Campbell
steps.text: Honeyberry, you're back—wait, why did you bring—

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Don't worry, Mrs. Campbell. Infected in stable condition are not contagious.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Lydia is living proof. She's been staying with the Infected for so long, but she never caught Oripathy.

steps.name: Campbell
steps.text: Really? But why does she look so sickly then?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Ah... that's why we came back. Let's just say that she's lovesick.

steps.name: Campbell
steps.text: Lovesick? Now this I need to hear.

steps.name: Campbell
steps.text: Aha. So that's what this is about.

steps.name: Campbell
steps.text: Now why the heck didn't you let your sister come back and see her boyfriend, Gus?

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: It was you people who—

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Gus had his own troubles to deal with, ma'am. No one knew where the Oripathy came from, did they?

steps.name: Campbell
steps.text: So, who's the lucky young man who caught Lydia's eye?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Sorry, I've got a non-disclosure agreement with Gus.

steps.name: Campbell
steps.text: How could you do that, Gus?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Don't blame him. It's natural for him to be a little resentful after his exile from the village.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Besides, there's no real point if the young man isn't willing to step forward of his own accord, is there?

steps.name: Campbell
steps.text: You've got me there. Alright, I'll get everyone.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: (Whisper) Is Carl here, Lydia? I don't remember how he looks.
Still with a fever, Lydia bites her lip while casting her gaze towards a young man in a corner.
He stands beside Martenson, looking slightly timid. His father's eyes are wary as they meet Honeyberry's.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: ...Step forward, if you still love her.
The crowd whispers amongst themselves. Some parents ask their children, while others ask Martenson, who shakes his head furiously.
Carl stands behind his father, his expression hidden from view.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: The sickness of your beloved isn't because of Oripathy. It's because she misses you.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: She insisted on coming back to see you. Please, step forward!
Martenson starts getting impatient and turns to leave, while Carl seems to be nailed to the ground.

steps.name: Martenson
steps.text: Oripathy has fried the girl's brain. Get her out of here!
Honeyberry thought she would hear objections from the crowd, but there were none.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Guys...

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: What are you afraid of?

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: Don't bother, Honeyberry. They won't listen.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: No! I have to speak up!

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: The kids all love Mrs. Campbell because she always makes biscuits for them.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Mrs. Samantha doesn't trust people easily, but when she does, she always stands up for them.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: The Martenson family works hard to live a better life, without forgetting to help out their neighbors.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: This village is full of good people. What kind of deep, heavy—evil fear could make you all so heartless and cruel?

spans.text: This village is full of good people. What kind of deep, heavy—
fear could make you all so heartless and cruel?

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: ...That's enough, Zoey.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Lydia?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: But you haven't seen your boyfriend yet.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: (Smiles meekly)

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: I saw him. I did.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: He heard you scold everyone, and he stayed here in opposition to his family's wishes... The important thing is that I saw him, and he saw me.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: I know he loves me. He just can't... I don't blame him. How can I?

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: It's enough, Zoey. I'm happy enough.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: I don't want to make his life difficult, even if I'm not Infected.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: We...

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: We—

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: (Sobs)

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Let's go...

steps.name: Martenson
steps.text: Carl?! Are you out of your mind? Where are you going?
Carl hugs the weakened Lydia in his arms.

steps.name: Carl
steps.text: I swear I won't ever leave you again, Lydia.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Am... am I dreaming, Carl? It's a dream, right?

steps.name: Carl
steps.text: No, it's not a dream!

steps.name: Carl
steps.text: I almost lost you once. No one will ever keep us apart again!

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: (Rubs eyes)

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: You see, Gus? Just like I said.

steps.name: Gus
steps.text: Carl...
Honeyberry casts her gaze at the crowd and feels her heart sink.
Campbell is wiping tears from her eyes, but not many others are rejoicing for the young lovers.
More prevalent are expressions of hesitation, doubt, and fear.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Excuse me...
Honeyberry feels a chill run down her back at the cold reaction of the crowd.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Will you accept Lydia back into the village?
She said 'Lydia' rather than 'the Infected,' without even realizing it.
A moment of silence passes.
Finally, someone opens his mouth.

steps.name: Martenson
steps.text: Think about it carefully, Carl.

steps.name: Martenson
steps.text: Go with her, and you can never come back.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Martenson
steps.text: It can't be helped.
Honeyberry feels a daze come over her.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Wh-What are you talking about? So many years have passed. Haven't we proven ourselves healthy by now?

steps.name: Lydia's Grandfather
steps.text: People are afraid, Zoey.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: What are they afraid of?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: They forced dad out! He's not around anymore! Mum and I have lived in the forest for so many years! What makes them so afraid that we can't even set foot in the village?

steps.name: Lydia's Grandfather
steps.text: It can't be helped.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: It can't be helped? Is that your final answer?

steps.name: Samantha
steps.text: Better safe than sorry, after all.

steps.name: Samantha
steps.text: How about this: I won't try to get Gus to pay for all the stuff he broke and all the lost business. We'll just leave each other alone going forward.

steps.name: Samantha
steps.text: That way, he won't come and cause any more trouble, right?

steps.name: Samantha
steps.text: Just have them go back. Once they're gone, the village will owe you a feast. Everyone appreciates how you took care of the problem.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: But I've already said that Oripathy patients in stable condition aren't—

steps.name: Samantha
steps.text: Just let it go, okay? Who knows who's Infected or not when they're not growing any rocks?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Rhodes Island is sending over equipment for Oripathy screening and testing, and our staff will be teaching people how to use it. Isn't that enough to dispel your fear?

steps.name: Samantha
steps.text: That... that's in the future. What if there's a delay? What if there's an equipment error?

steps.name: Samantha
steps.text: Just let it go, and let them go. I'll make you my special—

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Mille-feuille.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Mrs. Samantha, I...

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: I'm Zoey Perris.
A commotion spreads through the crowd.

steps.name: Samantha
steps.text: Perris... You're Perris's girl, Zoey? You're not Infected?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Like I said, Oripathy is not transmissible the way the flu is. Plus, Dad—

steps.name: Martenson
steps.text: Get out! The children of the Infected are not welcome here!

steps.name: Campbell
steps.text: What are you talking about, Martenson?

steps.name: Martenson
steps.text: Perris was the first Infected in the village! How could we let his daughter in here?

steps.name: Campbell
steps.text: Didn't she just say that Oripathy isn't transmitted like that?

steps.name: Martenson
steps.text: Can she say for sure? Is she the one who'll have to pay the price if we have new Infected?

steps.name: Frightened Crowd
steps.text: Yeah, yeah!

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: I—
Honeyberry feels a lump in her throat and could say no more.
Martenson's attitude is harsh and stern, but Honeyberry sees only fear in his eyes.
The same fear that they had cast towards her family.
She looks around at Samantha, at the others, and sees the same in their eyes.

steps.name: Sandwheel
steps.text: Honeyberry.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: ...Sandwheel?

steps.name: Sandwheel
steps.text: Don't forget what we're here for.

steps.name: Sandwheel
steps.text: We're not here to promote proper Oripathy prevention and treatment, nor are we here to dispel their prejudices.

steps.name: Sandwheel
steps.text: We're just here to resolve the Infected problem.

steps.name: Sandwheel
steps.text: You've done what you could. Leave the rest to the operators delivering the equipment.

steps.name: Sandwheel
steps.text: Our job now is to worry about Gus's group, and that pair of lovers.

steps.name: Sandwheel
steps.text: Feeling better?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: (Blows nose)

steps.name: Sandwheel
steps.text: Think about happier things.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Happier things?

steps.name: Sandwheel
steps.text: Like about how Rhodes Island is opening an office in the nearest Rim Billiton nomadic city, and how they'll need new staff to run it.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: ...Yes, we're lucky that Gus and the other two Infected have somewhere to go.

steps.name: Sandwheel
steps.text: Lydia is recovering quickly, and she and Carl are applying to a mining company branch in the city. Isn't that something to be happy about?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Yeah...

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Now I'm realizing that the village never changed.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Not once, from the day they ran out our family, to the day Dad passed away, to the day I came to Rhodes Island with Mum, and all the way till today.

steps.name: Sandwheel
steps.text: Most villages that small never change. That one just happens to lie on the supply route for a new Originium mine.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: But this event... could it be the catalyst for change in the future?

steps.name: Sandwheel
steps.text: Mind if I said something that you might not like to hear?

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Go ahead.

steps.name: Sandwheel
steps.text: Change was inevitable the moment ore deposits were found in the area.

steps.name: Sandwheel
steps.text: The village has to either change, or perish.

steps.name: Sandwheel
steps.text: You were still willing to come back and help them. That alone ought to push them to set aside old prejudices and fears.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: I'm jumping, Mint!

steps.name: Mint
steps.text: Alright, I'm down here for you—

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Phew.

steps.name: Mint
steps.text: I was really worried when you came back from that field mission looking like a different person.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Just had a little bit of a shock. Got over it real quick, though.

steps.name: Mint
steps.text: By the way, there was a letter for you yesterday. The Messenger left it with me when they couldn't find you.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: From where?

steps.name: Mint
steps.text: Rim Billiton. Here.

steps.name: Mint
steps.text: I'm off for training. Feel free to join me after you read it.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: Sure!
Dear Zoey,
How are you doing?
Carl and I both applied to the mining company. Guess who got hired?
Both of us! I couldn't believe it!
We celebrated by having a nice meal out. Carl chose a Siracusan restaurant, and it was really good. We'll take you there next time you're here.
We both went through the entrance physical, and showed no trace of Oripathy. I've fully recovered from my symptoms too.
Thank you so much for your help.
Give your mum my regards!
Your dearest Lydia
P.S.: Carl's dad came to see him and brought him some food from home.
He said that the arguments went on for days after the Rhodes Island operators brought the Oripathy screening equipment and trained people how to use it.
In the end, they're letting the Infected and their families live near the village. They don't have to stay in the forest anymore.
He asked whether we wanted to go back, but Carl turned him down.
Even if Carl said yes, though, I wouldn't go back. I won't ever go back.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: I guess I don't have to go back anymore.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: They've taken the first step. They'll put their prejudices aside.

steps.name: Honeyberry
steps.text: They will.
